title: Run lease
description: Version 1 lease of one store resource (ADR-0025 decision 1, #223): its owner, its authoritative expiry decided by the store clock, and its exact monotonically increasing epoch. The fence is the evidence a writer presents at every checkpoint commit and an effect host checks at every admission. A lease grants neither tool permission nor approval. A released or expired lease is never revived; the next acquisition takes a strictly greater epoch. Version 2 (ADR-0029) is a delegated run's lease: it holds the run's principals (principal), a takeover is a new epoch of the same principals and any other is refused principal-changed; version 1 names none and cannot host a delegated run.

state.description: held: the owner holds it until its expiry. released: the owner gave it up; the epoch is retained so the next acquisition is greater. Expired is not stored: the store clock decides it at every check, and an expiry equal to the store's time is expired.

principal.description: Version 2 only, and required there (the readers hold it): the delegated run's subject, root actor and issuing host.

identifier.description: An opaque storage identifier: 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes, no control characters.

epoch.description: The exact epoch: a canonical base-10 integer string from 1 to 999999999999999999 (at most 18 digits, no sign, no leading zero, no fraction or exponent). It fits a signed 64-bit integer exactly and is never carried as a JSON number, so no reader rounds it. Acquiring past the largest epoch refuses as epoch-exhausted.

expiry.description: The authoritative expiry, decided by the store clock: UTC with exactly millisecond precision.

fence.description: The fence: the evidence a writer presents at a checkpoint commit and an effect host checks at an admission. It is current when the store holds a lease of the resource with this owner and exactly this epoch, not released and not expired by the store clock. A version 2 fence names the delegated run's principals, which must be the lease's: a takeover or dispatch under others is refused principal-changed.

principal.description: Version 2 only, and required there (the readers hold it): the delegated run's subject, root actor and issuing host.

operation.description: The stable idempotency identity of one effect: the run, the operation's claim identity, its target (source and tool) and the request digest. It carries no epoch, so a takeover cannot turn the same uncertain operation into a new action.

effectAdmission.description: What an effect host receives before it performs an effect: the fence and the operation. idempotencyKey is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the operation alone.

refusal.description: A named lease or fence refusal. Nothing was admitted or committed. already-admitted is an effect host's answer to an idempotency identity it admitted before: that outcome stays unknown and is never performed again. principal-changed: a takeover or fence under another subject or root actor than the lease holds (ADR-0029).

capabilityRefusal.description: A store or effect host that cannot give the lease and fence guarantee refuses unattended admission by name, before any dispatch. store-unsupported: the store has no lease port. store-lifetime: its leases end with its process. effect-host-unfenced: no effect host, or one that does not enforce the fence.
